Shared PLE key gate ne0=2560, ne1=10240, elements=26214400 precedes both native and unquantized wiring; prior pointer/type/BF16 byte checks retained.
Require opened table rows()==kernels::PLE_TABLE_ROWS (320001536) before wiring or inference.

Bare duplicate-rejected --validation-small-input flag admits only 1..32767; absent flag retains 32768..262144. Context>=8192, context>=count, context<=262144 and chunk8192 remain mandatory. Immutable const Options controls validation_small_input and measurement_scope receipt fields. Single-token predecessor is -1; normal first length uses min(chunk,count). Existing optional short-first dispatch retained.

After existing queue retirement and session_release, free each allocated QSA state host_step/host_pos through borrowed allocation queue, then clear pointers before descriptor deletion. Include partial-init nonnull fields.
After successful write/flush, release FILE unique_ptr ownership into exactly one checked fclose; close failure throws before success receipt, with no double close and no fsync.

source_review.method: Read-only source/Git/hash inspection, complete two-file patch review; Python3 only edits/hashes/metadata generation. No product code executed.
source_review.main_sha_scope: SHA evidence function only, not native engine/provider/numerical/256K/historical600 qualification

exception_review: Before session initialization, qsa_states is null; session_init value-initializes full geometry descriptors before per-state allocation. All qsa_alloc slots are inspected, including partially initialized and untouched null states. This harness uses the full session with qsa_ord0=0; no split-session generalization is claimed.

QSA staging malloc_host uses dpct::get_in_order_queue(); allocation=q_of(nullptr) is that borrowed checked default queue. No device switch occurs between initialization and cleanup. Compute and allocation are retired before the new frees; allocation remains live until after all frees. Owning compute alone is destroyed last.

Queue uncertainty preserves existing fail-stop86, delivered checked async errors87, cleanup exceptions/terminate88. A free exception stops the process before deletion or success; this is not a promise of complete reclamation on provider failure.

Capture open failure has no live stream; write/flush failure unwinds unique_ptr once and remains failure even if destructor close also fails. Successful write/flush enters checked fclose(file.release()); close failure cannot double-close and reaches ordinary failure before receipt. Failed partial capture is not removed by this delivery.

Provider partial-acceptance, allocator/free correctness, asynchronous error delivery and external library unwind behavior remain unexecuted dependencies. Source control-flow review does not certify them.
